1.en: When the imminent Event comes to pass when the Resurrection takes place
1.ar:
سُورَة الواقِعَة [ مَكِّيَّة إلّا آيَتَيْ ٨١ و ٨٢ فَمَدَنِيَّتانِ ] "وآياتها ٩٦ و ٩٧ و ٩٩"

﴿إذا وقَعَتْ الواقِعَة﴾ قامَتْ القِيامَة

2.en: there will be no denying its coming to pass there is no soul to deny it by repudiating it as it did in this world
2.ar: ﴿لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِها كاذِبَة﴾ نَفْس تَكْذِب بِأَنْ تَنْفِيها كَما نَفَتْها فِي الدُّنْيا

3.en: it will be abasing some exalting others that is it will manifest the abasing of some people by virtue of their admission into the Fire and manifest the exalting of others by their admission into Paradise.
3.ar: ﴿خافِضَة رافِعَة﴾ أيْ هِيَ مُظْهِرَة لِخَفْضِ أقْوام بِدُخُولِهِمْ النّار ولِرَفْعِ آخَرِينَ بِدُخُولِهِمْ الجَنَّة

4.en: When the earth is shaken with a violent shock
4.ar: ﴿إذا رُجَّتْ الأَرْض رَجًّا﴾ حُرِّكَتْ حَرَكَة شَدِيدَة وإذا هَذِهِ بَدَل مِن الأُولى

5.en: and the mountains are pulverised to tiny pieces

6.en: so that they become a scattered dust the second idh ‘when’ is a substitution for the first idh

7.en: and you will be at the Resurrection three kinds categories

8.en: Those of the right hand those who are given their record of deeds in their right hand fa-ashābu’l-maymanati is the subject the predicate of which is the following mā ashābu’l-maymanati — what of those of the right hand? — a glorification of their status on account of their admittance into Paradise.
8.ar: ﴿فَأَصْحاب المَيْمَنَة﴾ وهُمْ الَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ كُتُبهمْ بِأَيْمانِهِمْ مُبْتَدَأ خَبَره ﴿ما أصْحاب المَيْمَنَة﴾ تَعْظِيم لِشَأْنِهِمْ بِدُخُولِهِمْ الجَنَّة

9.en: And those of the left hand al-mash’ama means al-shimāl ‘left’ each of whom is given his record of deeds in their left hands — what of those of the left hand? — an expression of contempt for their status on account of their admittance into the Fire.
9.ar: ﴿وأَصْحاب المَشْأَمَة﴾ أيْ الشِّمال بِأَنْ يُؤْتى كُلّ مِنهُمْ كِتابه بِشِمالِهِ ﴿ما أصْحاب المَشْأَمَة﴾ تَحْقِير لِشَأْنِهِمْ بِدُخُولِهِمْ النّار

10.en: And the foremost in the race to do good namely the prophets al-sābiqūna is a subject the foremost this repetition is to emphasise their exalted status; the predicate is the following ūlā’ika’l-muqarrabūna
10.ar: ﴿والسّابِقُونَ﴾ إلى الخَيْر وهُمْ الأَنْبِياء مُبْتَدَأ ﴿السّابِقُونَ﴾ تَأْكِيد لِتَعْظِيمِ شَأْنهمْ

11.en: they are the ones brought near to God

13.en: a multitude from the former generations thullatun mina’l-awwalīna the subject that is to say a group of individuals from communities of old
13.ar: ﴿ثُلَّة مِن الأَوَّلِينَ﴾ مُبْتَدَأ أيْ جَماعَة مِن الأُمَم الماضِيَة

14.en: and a few from the later ones from among the community of Muhammad (s) being the foremost from among the communities of old and this community the predicate is the following ‘alā sururin mawdūnatin
14.ar: ﴿وقَلِيل مِن الآخِرِينَ﴾ مِن أُمَّة مُحَمَّد ﷺ وهُمْ السّابِقُونَ مِن الأُمَم الماضِيَة وهَذِهِ الأُمَّة والخَبَر

15.en: will be upon encrusted couches their linings woven onto rods of gold and jewels
15.ar: ﴿عَلى سُرَر مَوْضُونَة﴾ مَنسُوجَة بِقُضْبانِ الذَّهَب والجَواهِر

16.en: reclining on them face to face muttaki’īna ‘alayhā mutaqābilīna constitute two circumstantial qualifiers referring to the subject person of the predicate ‘they’.
16.ar: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَيْها مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾ حالانِ مِن الضَّمِير فِي الخَبَر

17.en: They will be waited on by immortal youths resembling young boys never ageing;
17.ar: ﴿يَطُوف عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ لِلْخِدْمَةِ ﴿وِلْدان مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ عَلى شَكْل الأَوْلاد لا يَهْرَمُونَ

18.en: with goblets akwāb are drinking-vessels without handles and ewers abārīq are vessels that have handles and spouts and a cup ka’s is the vessel for drinking wine from a flowing spring in other words wine flowing from a spring that never runs out
18.ar: ﴿بِأَكْوابٍ﴾ أقْداح لا عُرا لَها ﴿وأَبارِيق﴾ لَها عُرا وخَراطِيم ﴿وكَأْس﴾ إناء شُرْب الخَمْر ﴿مِن مَعِين﴾ أيْ خَمْر جارِيَة مِن مَنبَع لا يَنْقَطِع أبَدًا

19.en: wherefrom they suffer no headache nor any stupefaction read yanzafūna or yanzifūna respectively derived from nazafa or anzafa al-shāribu ‘the drinker became inebriated’ in other words they do not get a headache from it nor do they lose their senses in contrast to the case with the wine of this world;
19.ar: ﴿لا يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْها ولا يُنْزَفُونَ﴾ بِفَتْحِ الزّاي وكَسْرها مِن نَزَفَ الشّارِب وأَنْزَفَ أيْ لا يَحْصُل لَهُمْ مِنها صُداع ولا ذَهاب عَقْل بِخِلافِ خَمْر الدُّنْيا

20.en: and such fruits as they prefer

21.en: and such flesh of fowls as they desire for themselves to enjoy

22.en: and houris maidens with intensely black eyes set against the whiteness of their irises with wide eyes ‘īn the ‘ayn here is inflected with a kasra instead of a damma because it the kasra better harmonises with the yā’; the singular is ‘aynā’ similar in pattern to hamrā’; a variant reading for wa-hūrun ‘īn has the genitive case wa-hūrin ‘īn
22.ar: ﴿وحُور﴾ نِساء شَدِيدات سَواد العُيُون وبَياضها ﴿عِين﴾ ضِخام العُيُون كُسِرَتْ عَيْنه بَدَل ضَمّها لِمُجانَسَةِ الياء ومُفْرَده عَيْناء كَحَمْراء وفِي قِراءَة بِجَرِّ حُور عِين

24.en: a reward jazā’an is an object denoting reason or a verbal noun with the operator being an implicit verb in other words ‘We have appointed for them the mentioned as a reward’ or ‘We have rewarded them this’ for what they used to do.
24.ar: ﴿جَزاء﴾ مَفْعُول لَهُ أوْ مَصْدَر والعامِل المُقَدَّر أيْ جَعَلْنا لَهُمْ ما ذُكِرَ لِلْجَزاءِ أوْ جَزَيْناهُمْ

25.en: They will not hear therein in Paradise any vain talk any lewd words or any sinful words
25.ar: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها﴾ فِي الجَنَّة ﴿لَغْوًا﴾ فاحِشًا مِن الكَلام ﴿ولا تَأْثِيمًا﴾ ما يُؤْثِم

26.en: but only the saying ‘Peace!’ ‘Peace!’ salāman salāman substitutes for qīlan ‘the saying’ which they will hear.
26.ar: ﴿إلّا﴾ لَكِنْ ﴿قِيلًا﴾ قَوْلًا ﴿سَلامًا سَلامًا﴾ بَدَل مِن قِيلًا فَإنَّهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَهُ

27.en: And those of the right hand — what of those of the right hand?

28.ar: ﴿فِي سِدْر﴾ شَجَر النَّبْق ﴿مَخْضُود﴾ لا شَوْك فِيهِ

29.en: and clustered plantains banana trees weighed down with its load of fruit from top to bottom
29.ar: ﴿وطَلْح﴾ شَجَر المَوْز ﴿مَنضُود﴾ بِالحَمْلِ مِن أسْفَله إلى أعْلاهُ

30.en: and extended shade one that is permanent

33.en: neither unavailable during certain times nor forbidden because of its cost

34.en: and mattresses that are raised on top of couches.

35.en: Verily We have created them with an unmediated creation namely the wide-eyed houris We created them without the process of birth
35.ar: ﴿إنّا أنْشَأْناهُنَّ إنْشاء﴾ أيْ الحُور العِين مِن غَيْر وِلادَة

36.en: and made them virgins immaculate — every time their spouses enter them they find them virgins nor is there any pain of defloration —
36.ar: ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُنَّ أبْكارًا﴾ عَذارى كُلَّما أتاهُنَّ أزْواجهنَّ وجَدُوهُنَّ عَذارى ولا وجَع

37.en: amorous read ‘uruban or ‘urban plural of ‘arūb meaning ‘a woman passionately enamoured of her spouse’ of equal age atrāb is the plural of tirb
37.ar: ﴿عُرُبًا﴾ بِضَمِّ الرّاء وسُكُونها جَمْع عُرُوب وهِيَ المُتَحَبِّبَة إلى زَوْجها عِشْقًا لَهُ ﴿أتْرابًا﴾ جَمْع تِرْب أيْ مُسْتَوِيات فِي السِّنّ

38.en: for those of the right hand li-ashābi’l-yamīni is the relative clause of either ansha’nāhunna ‘We have created them’ or ja‘alnāhunna ‘We made them’ who are
38.ar: ﴿لِأَصْحابِ اليَمِين﴾ صِلَة أنْشَأْناهُنَّ أوْ جَعَلْناهُنَّ وهُمْ: ﴿ثُلَّة مِن الأَوَّلِينَ وثُلَّة مِن الآخِرِينَ﴾

39.en: A multitude from the former generations

40.en: and a multitude of the later ones.

41.en: And those of the left hand — what of those of the left hand?

42.en: Amid a scorching wind an infernal wind permeating the pores of skins and scalding water water of extreme temperatures
42.ar: ﴿فِي سَمُوم﴾ رِيح حارَّة مِن النّار تَنْفُذ فِي المَسامّ ﴿وحَمِيم﴾ ماء شَدِيد الحَرارَة

43.en: and the shade of pitch-black smoke

44.en: neither cool like all other shade nor pleasant nor agreeable in its appearance.
44.ar: ﴿لا بارِد﴾ كَغَيْرِهِ مِن الظِّلال ﴿ولا كَرِيم﴾ حَسَن المَنظَر

45.en: Indeed before that in the world they used to live at ease enjoying life’s comforts never wearying themselves with an act of obedience
45.ar: ﴿إنّهُمْ كانُوا قَبْل ذَلِك﴾ فِي الدُّنْيا ﴿مُتْرَفِينَ﴾ مُنَعَّمِينَ لا يَتْعَبُونَ فِي الطّاعَة

46.en: and they used to persist in the great sin namely idolatry.
46.ar: ﴿وكانُوا يُصِرُّونَ عَلى الحِنْث﴾ الذَّنْب ﴿العَظِيم﴾ أيْ الشِّرْك

47.en: And they used to say ‘What! When we are dead and have become dust and bones shall we indeed be resurrected? in both instances a-idhā and a-innā the two hamzas may be read either by pronouncing them fully or by not pronouncing the second and in either case inserting an intervening alif.
47.ar: ﴿وكانُوا يَقُولُونَ أإذا مِتْنا وكُنّا تُرابًا وعِظامًا أإنّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾ فِي الهَمْزَتَيْنِ فِي المَوْضِعَيْنِ التَّحْقِيق وتَسْهِيل الثّانِيَة وإدْخال ألِف بَيْنهما عَلى الوَجْهَيْنِ

48.en: What! And our forefathers too?’ read a-wa-ābā’unā with the wa- being for supplement the hamza a- for the interrogative; here and in the previous instance it is used to express ‘remoteness of probability’; a variant reading has aw-ābā’unā as a supplement with aw and that to which this is supplemented is the syntactical locus of inna and its subject.
48.ar: ﴿أوَ آباؤُنا الأَوَّلُونَ﴾ بِفَتْحِ الواو لِلْعَطْفِ والهَمْزَة لِلِاسْتِفْهامِ وهُوَ فِي ذَلِكَ وفِيما قَبْله لِلِاسْتِبْعادِ وفِي قِراءَة بِسُكُونِ الواو عَطْفًا بِأَوْ والمَعْطُوف عَلَيْهِ مَحَلّ إنّ واسْمها

49.en: Say ‘Truly the former and the later generations

50.en: will be gathered for the tryst the time of a known day that is the Day of Resurrection.
50.ar: ﴿لَمَجْمُوعُونَ إلى مِيقات﴾ لِوَقْتِ ﴿يَوْم مَعْلُوم﴾ أيْ يَوْم القِيامَة

51.en: Then indeed you the erring the deniers

52.en: will assuredly eat from a Zaqqūm tree min zaqqūm the explication of shajar ‘tree’
52.ar: ﴿لَآكِلُونَ مِن شَجَر مِن زَقُّوم﴾ بَيان لِلشَّجَرِ

53.en: and fill therewith with the tree your bellies

54.en: and drink on top of that the consumed Zaqqūm boiling water

55.en: drinking like the drinking read sharba or shurba verbal noun of thirsty camels’ hīm is the plural of masculine haymān and feminine haymā similar in pattern to ‘atshān ‘atshā ‘thirsty’.
55.ar: ﴿فَشارِبُونَ شَرْب﴾ بِفَتْحِ الشِّين وضَمّها مَصْدَر ﴿الهِيم﴾ الإبِل العِطاش جَمْع هَيْمان لِلذَّكَرِ وهَيْمى لِلْأُنْثى كَعَطْشان وعَطْشى

56.en: This will be the hospitality for them what has been prepared for them on the Day of Judgement the Day of Resurrection.
56.ar: ﴿هَذا نُزُلهمْ﴾ ما أُعِدَّ لَهُمْ ﴿يَوْم الدِّين﴾ يَوْم القِيامَة

57.en: We created you We brought you into existence from nothing. Will you not then affirm this truth? in resurrection? For the One able to create from nothing is also able to repeat this creation.
57.ar: ﴿نَحْنُ خَلَقْناكُمْ﴾ أوَجَدْناكُمْ مِن عَدَم ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ هَلّا ﴿تُصَدِّقُونَ﴾ بِالبَعْثِ إذْ القادِر عَلى الإنْشاء قادِر عَلى الإعادَة

58.en: Have you considered the sperm that you emit? the sperm you spill in the wombs of women?
58.ar: ﴿أفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تُمْنُونَ﴾ تُرِيقُونَ مِن المَنِيّ فِي أرْحام النِّساء

59.en: Is it you a-antum read by pronouncing both hamzas fully or by replacing the second one with an alif or not pronouncing it but inserting an alif between the one not pronounced and the other one or without this insertion in the four instances here and below who create it that is the sperm making it into a human being or are We the Creators?
59.ar: ﴿أأَنْتُمْ﴾ بِتَحْقِيقِ الهَمْزَتَيْنِ وإبْدال الثّانِيَة ألِفًا وتَسْهِيلها وإدْخال ألِف بَيْن المُسَهَّلَة والأُخْرى وتَرْكه فِي المَواضِع الأُخْرى ﴿تَخْلُقُونَهُ﴾ أيْ المَنِيّ بَشَرًا

60.en: We have ordained read qaddarnā or qadarnā death among you and We are not to be outmanoeuvred from We are not incapable of
60.ar: ﴿نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا﴾ بِالتَّشْدِيدِ والتَّخْفِيف ﴿بَيْنكُمْ المَوْت وما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ بِعاجِزِينَ

61.en: replacing you with We are not incapable of appointing your likes in your place and making you creating you in what you do not know in the way of forms such as apes or swine.
61.ar: ﴿عَلى﴾ عَنْ ﴿أنْ نُبَدِّل﴾ نَجْعَل ﴿أمْثالكُمْ﴾ مَكانكُمْ ﴿ونُنْشِئكُمْ﴾ نَخْلُقكُمْ ﴿فِي ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ مِن الصُّوَر كالقِرَدَةِ والخَنازِير

62.en: For verily you have known the first creation al-nashā’ata a variant reading has al-nash’ata why then will you not remember? tadhakkarūna the original second tā’ of tatadhakkarūna has been assimilated with the dhāl.
62.ar: ﴿ولَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ النَّشْأَة الأُولى﴾ وفِي قِراءَة بِسُكُونِ الشِّين ﴿فَلَوْلا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ فِيهِ إدْغام التّاء الثّانِيَة فِي الأَصْل فِي الذّال

63.en: Have you considered what you sow? what you stir of the earth to place seeds therein?
63.ar: ﴿أفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تَحْرُثُونَ﴾ تُثِيرُونَ فِي الأَرْض وتُلْقُونَ البَذْر فِيها

64.en: Is it you who make it grow or are We the Grower?

65.en: If We will We could surely turn it into chaff dried vegetation producing no seed and you would remain zaltum is actually zaliltum the lām having a kasra inflection; but it has been omitted to soften it that is to say you spend all day bemused tafakkahūna one of the original tā’ tatafakkahūna letters has been omitted surprised by this and you would say
65.ar: ﴿لَوْ نَشاء لَجَعَلْناهُ حُطامًا﴾ نَباتًا يابِسًا لا حَبّ فِيهِ ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ﴾ أصْله ظَلِلْتُمْ بِكَسْرِ اللّام حُذِفَتْ تَخْفِيفًا أيْ أقَمْتُمْ نَهارًا ﴿تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾ حُذِفَتْ مِنهُ إحْدى التّاءَيْنِ فِي الأَصْل تَعْجَبُونَ مِن ذَلِكَ وتَقُولُونَ:

66.en: ‘We have indeed suffered loss! losing what we expended on the cultivation.

67.en: Nay but we are deprived!’ prevented from reaping our provision.

68.en: Have you considered the water you drink?

69.en: Is it you who cause it to come down from the rain clouds muzn is the plural of muzna or are We the Causer of its coming down?
69.ar: ﴿أأَنْتُمْ أنَزَلْتُمُوهُ مِن المُزْن﴾ السَّحاب جَمْع مُزْنَة

70.en: If We willed We could make it bitter salty undrinkable — why then will you not give thanks?
70.ar: ﴿لَوْ نَشاء جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجًا﴾ مِلْحًا لا يُمْكِن شُرْبه ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ هَلّا

71.en: Have you considered the fire that you kindle? the fire which you produce out of the oil of green trees?
71.ar: ﴿أفَرَأَيْتُمْ النّار الَّتِي تُورُونَ﴾ تُخْرِجُونَ مِن الشَّجَر الأَخْضَر

72.en: Was it you who created the tree thereof trees such as the markh the ‘afār or the kalkh ‘fennel’ or were We the Creator?

73.en: We made it a reminder of the fire of Hell and a boon a provision for the desert-travellers al-muqwīn derives from the expression aqwā al-qawmu ‘they have reached al-qawā or al-qawā’ that is al-qafr ‘desolate land’ which is a wilderness mafāza that has neither vegetation nor water.
73.ar: ﴿نَحْنُ جَعَلْناها تَذْكِرَة﴾ لِنارِ جَهَنَّم ﴿ومَتاعًا﴾ بِلُغَةٍ ﴿لِلْمُقْوِينَ﴾ لِلْمُسافِرِينَ مِن أقْوى القَوْم: أيْ صارُوا بالقوا بِالقَصْرِ والمَدّ أيْ القَفْر وهُوَ مَفازَة لا نَبات فِيها ولا ماء

74.en: So glorify exalt the transcendence of the Name ism is extra of your Lord the Tremendous God.

75.en: Nay I swear fa-lā uqsimu lā is extra by the setting-places of the stars!
75.ar: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِم﴾ لا زائِدَة ﴿بِمَواقِع النُّجُوم﴾ بِمَساقِطِها لِغُرُوبِها

76.en: And indeed it the swearing by these setting-places of stars is a tremendous oath if you only knew — if you were people of deep knowledge you would realise the magnitude of this oath.
76.ar: ﴿وإنَّهُ﴾ أيْ القَسَم بِها ﴿لَقَسَم لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيم﴾ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ مِن ذَوِي العِلْم لَعَلِمْتُمْ عِظَم هَذا القَسَم

77.en: This namely what is being recited to you is indeed a noble Qur’ān

78.en: in a Book inscribed guarded preserved and this is the Mushaf;

79.en: which none touch lā yamassuhu is a predicate functioning as a prohibitive command except the purified those who have purified themselves of ritual impurities 5680 a revelation revealed by the Lord of the Worlds.
79.ar: ﴿لا يَمَسّهُ﴾ خَبَر بِمَعْنى النَّهْي ﴿إلّا المُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ الَّذِينَ طَهَّرُوا أنْفُسهمْ مِن الأَحْداث

80.en: Do you then belittle do you take lightly and deny this discourse? the Qur’ān.

81.en: And for your livelihood in the way of rain that is to say the thanks for it you offer your denial? of God’s granting it to you by saying ‘We have rain because of this or that storm’?

82.en: And for your livelihood in the way of rain that is to say the thanks for it you offer your denial? of God’s granting it to you by saying ‘We have rain because of this or that storm’?
82.ar: ﴿وتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقكُمْ﴾ مِن المَطَر أيْ شُكْره ﴿أنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ بِسُقْيا اللَّه حَيْثُ قُلْتُمْ مُطِرْنا بِنَوْءِ كَذا

83.en: Why then when it the spirit during the throes of death reaches the dying person’s throat hulqūm is the passage for food
83.ar: ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ فَهَلّا ﴿إذا بَلَغَتْ﴾ الرُّوح وقْت النَّزْع ﴿الحُلْقُوم﴾ هُوَ مَجْرى الطَّعام

84.en: and you are O you attending the dying person at that moment looking at him —
84.ar: ﴿وأَنْتُمْ﴾ يا حاضِرِي المَيِّت ﴿حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ تَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْهِ

85.en: and We are nearer to him than you are to know of his state but you do not perceive tubsirūna derives from al-basīra ‘perception’ that is to say you do not realise this —
85.ar: ﴿ونَحْنُ أقْرَب إلَيْهِ مِنكُمْ﴾ بِالعِلْمِ ﴿ولَكِنْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ مِن البَصِيرَة أيْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ ذَلِكَ

86.en: why then if you are not going to face a reckoning if you are not going to be requited by your being resurrected in other words why then if you are not going to be resurrected as you claim
86.ar: ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ فَهَلّا ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ غَيْر مَدِينِينَ﴾ مَجْزِيِّينَ بِأَنْ تُبْعَثُوا أيْ غَيْر مَبْعُوثِينَ بِزَعْمِكُمْ

87.en: do you not bring it back why do you not restore the spirit to the body after it has reached the throat if you are truthful? in what you claim the second law-lā ‘why … if’ is repeated to emphasise the first one; idhā ‘when’ is an adverbial particle qualifying tarji‘ūna ‘bring it back’ to which both conditions are semantically connected. The meaning is ‘Why do you not bring it back when in repudiating resurrection you are being truthful in this repudiation?’ That is to say ‘Let death also be repudiated as impossible in its case just as you claim that resurrection is impossible’.
87.ar: ﴿تَرْجِعُونَها﴾ تَرُدُّونَ الرُّوح إلى الجَسَد بَعْد بُلُوغ الحُلْقُوم ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ فِيما زَعَمْتُمْ فَلَوْلا الثّانِيَة تَأْكِيد لِلْأُولى وإذا ظَرْف لِتَرْجِعُونَ المُتَعَلِّق بِهِ الشَّرْطانِ والمَعْنى: هَلّا تَرْجِعُونَها إنْ نَفَيْتُمْ البَعْث صادِقِينَ فِي نَفْيه أيْ لِيَنْتَفِيَ عَنْ مَحِلّها المَوْت كالبَعْثِ

88.en: Thus if he the dead person be of those brought near

89.en: then repose that is there will be for him relief and a goodly provision and a garden of Bliss does this response belong to the ammā ‘thus’ or to in ‘if’ or to both? Different opinions are given regarding this.
89.ar: ﴿فَرَوْح﴾ أيْ فَلَهُ اسْتِراحَة ﴿ورَيْحان﴾ أيْ رِزْق حَسَن ﴿وجَنَّة نَعِيم﴾ وهَلْ الجَواب لِأَمّا أوْ لإنْ أوْ لَهُما ؟ أقْوال.

90.en: And if he be of those of the right hand

91.en: then ‘Peace be to you’ that is then for him there will be peace by way of security salām from chastisement a greeting from those of the right hand arising from the fact that he is one of them.
91.ar: ﴿فَسَلام لَك﴾ أيْ لَهُ السَّلامَة مِن العَذاب ﴿مِن أصْحاب اليَمِين﴾ مِن جِهَة أنَّهُ مِنهُمْ

92.en: But if he be of the deniers the erring

93.en: then a welcome of boiling water

95.en: This indeed is the certain truth haqqu’l-yaqīn an example of an adjectivally qualified noun being annexed to its adjective.
95.ar: ﴿إنّ هَذا لَهُوَ حَقّ اليَقِين﴾ مِن إضافَة المَوْصُوف إلى صِفَته

96.en: So glorify the Name of your Lord the Tremendous as explained above in verse 74.
